subject: Side-by-side bakeoff synthesis & validation plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@novacare.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacare.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11 14:03 -0700
Subject: Side-by-side bakeoff synthesis & validation plan

Thanks for taking time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the decision criteria you emphasized, and the validation tests we propose for the side-by-side. I left action owners and target dates so we can keep momentum.

Highlights (pain points you confirmed)
- Latency unpredictability at high concurrencies: 95th pct spikes during weekday peak causing user-facing lag.
- Token cost is a major procurement lever — you need predictable unit economics for forecasting.
- Data residency & audit logs are mandatory for the pilot (HIPAA-adjacent workflows).
- Model parity: want output comparability versus current vendor for the 12 most common clinical prompts.

Top goals
1) Prove 95th-pct latency <= 350ms for the 512-token persona workload at 200 rps.
2) Demonstrate either equivalent quality or clear metric-based tradeoffs (ROUGE/EM/clinician acceptability) for templates.
3) Produce an apples-to-apples cost projection for 1M tokens/day over a 6-month run.

Decision criteria you prioritized (in order)
1. Latency & reliability under load
2. Deterministic cost model + observability
3. Output quality on clinical prompts
4. Security/compliance posture (KMS, audit logs)

Proposed validation tests (what we will run)
- Perf parity: 24-hour run vs. your current vendor at 200 rps, 512-token median workload. Metric: 50/90/95/99 latencies, error rate. (Owner: Rishi; ETA: 2026-10-13)
- Quality probe: 12 templated prompts + 30 open examples scored by your clinical SME set. Metric: pairwise preference + acceptance threshold. (Owner: NovaCare / Priya; Redwood to provide scoring sheet)
- Cost projection: run token-instrumented trial and produce per-1M token cost with batching/quantization knobs applied. (Owner: Aisha; ETA: 2026-10-15)
- Security checklist: deliver audit log samples, KMS integration plan, and SOC-like evidence stub. (Owner: Camila; ETA: 2026-10-14)

Attachments: novacare-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (template + scoring rubric), redwood-validation-test-plan.pdf (test matrix + runbook)

Next concrete steps
- Rishi will kick off the perf parity job on Tuesday; target first 6-hour smoke run by 2026-10-13.
- Priya: share clinical SME scoring slot and the 12 canonical prompts by 2026-10-12 end of day.
- Procurement: confirm any non-standard contract terms flagged during pilot by 2026-10-16.

If that aligns, we will stand up the tests and share a live dashboard so you can watch the metrics in real time. Appreciate the openness on tradeoffs during the call — that helped prioritize the tests.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@novacare.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacare.com>, procurement@novacare.com
Date: 2026-10-11 16:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Side-by-side bakeoff synthesis & validation plan

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) On latency targets: 350ms 95th is aspirational; if Redwood can reliably stay under 450ms at 200 rps that would still be compelling given current vendor variability. Please include p95 and p99 in the dashboard.
2) On cost: procurement wants a 6-month committed-run projection and a breakout of expected savings with and without quantization (we have rules about model determinism).
3) For quality scoring, Priya will distribute the clinical prompts and an initial set of 30 de-identified examples tomorrow. Can you confirm you will not retain the raw examples? We need an explicit note on data handling for legal.

Also, could you add a small head-to-head for hallucination rate on the clinical Q&A prompts? We'll need simple failure-mode flags.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll watch for the test plan PDF and the scorecard.

—Liam
Director of Product, NovaCare

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12 09:07 -0700
Subject: Internal: NovaCare asks + runbook adjustments

Internal note — copying the asks into the runbook: 
- Add p99/latency and hallucination probe to the test matrix.
- Rishi: prioritize a 6-hour smoke run with full KV cache enabled and with/without int8 quantization so we can surface quality deltas quickly. If int8 causes non-determinism for a specific clinical prompt set, capture that as part of the quality table.
- Camila to prepare a one-page data handling note (no retention of raw clinical examples; ephemeral logs stored only for debugging for 72 hours unless otherwise required) to send to Liam + legal.

I also suggest adding a lightweight competitor check: run the same 6-hour smoke with Competitor X's public endpoint (rate-limited) to get a direct latency delta. We won't store their outputs beyond immediate scoring.

I'll fold these into the redwood-validation-test-plan.pdf and re-attach.

-Camila
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@novacare.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacare.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13 09:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Side-by-side bakeoff synthesis & validation plan — perf smoke scheduled

Liam / Priya — quick update from the infra side: we've scheduled the 6-hour smoke perf run to start 2026-10-13 17:00 UTC (that's 10:00 PT) with the following variants:
- Baseline: Redwood default runtime, KV cache ON, no quantization
- Quantized: int8 path enabled (best-effort determinism check)
- Competitor X: lightweight parity check against public endpoint (rate-limited)

What we'll surface in the live dashboard: 50/90/95/99 latencies, error rates, token throughput, and a hallucination counter for the clinical QA probe (we'll compute simple mismatch flags and provide raw diffs in the scorecard).

I'll post the live dashboard link once the run starts and attach interim CSVs to the shared Drive folder. We will not persist your raw examples beyond the debugging window — Camila will send the data-handling note formally in a follow-up.

If you want the smoke run earlier, tell us today and we can attempt a morning slot but priority infra work means 10:00 PT is the earliest stable window.

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
